Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1) Manage presumed acute infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk: emphasize hydration, monitor for fever, avoid antibiotics, and stay home until symptoms improve; arrange GP visit if symptoms worsen or fail to improve.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for 3 days with central abdominal pain and vomiting; frequent urge to use the toilet; feels near-constant to close proximity to toilet.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began ~3 days ago.
- Course: Diarrhea ongoing (neither clearly improving nor worsening); abdominal pain present; vomiting occurred this morning; no persistent fever reported; no clear blood in stool or vomit.
- Associated symptoms: No chest pain; able to walk and talk; able to eat small amounts intermittently; appears to be eating fruit earlier today but not eating much due to GI symptoms.
- PMH: Asthma; uses inhaler (brand noted as possibly new).
- Allergies: NKDA (no known drug allergies) as reported.
- Medications: Inhaler for asthma; dose/route/frequency not documented; possible new brand.
- Social history: Not documented.
- Family history: Father died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago; patient expresses worry about personal risk.

Objective:
- General/appearance: Patient able to communicate clearly; walking and talking OK.
- Abdominal exam: Central abdominal pain; mild tenderness on palpation.
- GI symptoms: Diarrhea described as frequent (near every 10 minutes at times); vomiting earlier today (no current vomiting documented); no obvious blood in stool or vomit reported; abdomen tenderness elicited on palpation.
- Respiratory: History of asthma; uses inhaler; no acute respiratory distress described.
- Vital signs: Not provided.
- Other: No chest pain reported.

Assessment & Plan:

1) Acute gastroenteritis with diarrhea, abdominal pain, and intermittent vomiting
- Assessment: Most consistent with infectious gastroenteritis as per clinician’s impression.
- Differential diagnoses: Viral or food-borne gastroenteritis; less likely structural bowel disease given acute onset and current symptoms.
- Investigations planned: None at this time.
- Treatment planned:
  - Advise increased fluid intake and oral hydration to prevent dehydration.
  - Avoid routine antibiotics; antibiotics not recommended for this presentation unless indicated by clinical course.
  - Stay home while symptoms persist and gradually return to normal activities as tolerated.
  - Monitor for fever or worsening symptoms; seek in-person GP evaluation if symptoms worsen or do not improve.
- Referrals: None.

2) Anxiety related to family history of bowel cancer
- Assessment: Patient expresses concern about paternal history of bowel cancer; currently perceived as less likely related to the present illness.
- Differential diagnoses: Anxiety/family history concern.
- Investigations planned: None.
- Treatment planned:
  - Reassurance that current symptoms are more consistent with gastroenteritis.
  - If symptoms persist or worsen, discuss with GP for further evaluation of GI symptoms and family history implications.
- Relevant referrals: None.
